instructions.question: Does this Facebook comment on the Kosovo public health institute's COVID-19 post express warm approval or hope, an explicit hostile or distressed feeling, or neither (information, requests, suggestions, banter)?
instructions.rule: Neutral is the default. Requests for data, 'why' questions, demands for measures or more tests, comparisons with other countries, scolding of mask-skippers, sarcasm about testing and city 'league' banter stay neutral, even when critical. Choose negative only when the comment shows an explicit marker: assigning blame or fault, claiming the numbers are invented or fake, insulting people, saying they are fed up or tired, or expressing fear, horror or despair. Positive needs praise, thanks, relief at good numbers or hope for zero cases; praise mixed with criticism is still positive.

neutral.what: Tags, statistics, observations, requests for details, questions, proposals, mask reminders, comparisons, jokes and banter, including mildly critical or sarcastic ones.
examples: Mbyllni kufinjt mos luani me jetet e njerzve (Close the borders, don't play with people's lives)
Nëse nuk bëjmë asnjë test, s'do të kemi asnjë rast. U zgjidh problemi. (If we do no tests, we'll have no cases. Problem solved.)
Pse ka Mitrovica Verit nuk po jepni Rezultate hiq !? (Why aren't you giving any results for North Mitrovica!?)
Jeckpoot...vushtri e dhezi..apet (Jackpot... Vushtrri lit up again)
neutral.cues: personal names, publikoni (publish), testoni (test), mbyllni (close), pse (why), ma gjall (livelier), on top, hahaha
neutral.not_for: Explicit blame, claims of fake numbers, insults, being fed up, or fear are negative.

positive.what: Praise or thanks to doctors or the institute, congratulations, hope or prayers for no cases, cheering at recoveries.
examples: Respekt per punen tuaj (Respect for your work)
shpresoj qe ta kalojmë këtë gjendje me sa më pak pasoja. (I hope we get through this with as few consequences as possible.)
Ajde ma gjall ma gjall t sherum (Come on, more and more recovered)
positive.cues: bravo (well done), respekt (respect), faleminderit (thanks), urime (congratulations), shpresoj (I hope), inshallah (God willing), asnje rast (no cases), mir (good)
positive.not_for: 'Ma gjall' cheering of new infections is neutral.

negative.what: Blame of government or citizens, claims the numbers are invented, insults, fed-up frustration, fear or despair.
examples: Qeveria koti ika fajet (The Kurti government is to blame)
Veq shifren e par pja ndrroni se tekstin tjeter veq copy paste po get (You only change the first number, the rest is copy paste)
U ba bajat me ka 200 mo  ndrrone pak (It's stale with 200 a day, change it a bit)
Krejt Rrena (All lies)
negative.cues: faj (blame), rrena (lies), aparati (the machine), bajat (stale), lodhet (tired), merzit (fed up), injoranta (ignorant), katastrof (catastrophe), tmerr (horror), deshtim (failure)
negative.not_for: Requests, proposals, questions or banter without such a marker are neutral.
